questions.questionText: What is the main structural basis of a cell-surface membrane?
options: A phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins
A cellulose sheet with free DNA
questions.correctAnswer: A phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins
questions.explanation: The fluid-mosaic model describes a phospholipid bilayer containing proteins and other components.

curriculum.objective: Apply membrane, organelle and transport models to explain cell responses and energy-dependent processes.

questions.questionText: In osmosis, water moves across a partially permeable membrane in which direction?
options: From lower to higher pressure only
From higher to lower water potential
From higher to lower solute concentration in every case
questions.correctAnswer: From higher to lower water potential
questions.explanation: Net osmosis is movement of water from a region of higher water potential to lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane.

curriculum.objective: Apply membrane, organelle and transport models to explain cell responses and energy-dependent processes.

questions.questionText: Where is the electron transport chain for aerobic respiration located in a eukaryotic cell?
questions.correctAnswer: Inner mitochondrial membrane
questions.explanation: Electron carriers and ATP synthase are located in the inner mitochondrial membrane, including the cristae.

curriculum.objective: Apply membrane, organelle and transport models to explain cell responses and energy-dependent processes.

questions.questionText: Cyanide blocks the final electron carrier in aerobic respiration. What is the most immediate consequence?
options: Oxidative phosphorylation stops and ATP output falls sharply
questions.correctAnswer: Oxidative phosphorylation stops and ATP output falls sharply
questions.explanation: Blocking electron transfer prevents proton pumping and chemiosmosis, so mitochondrial ATP production rapidly collapses.

curriculum.objective: Apply membrane, organelle and transport models to explain cell responses and energy-dependent processes.

questions.questionText: What determines an enzyme active site’s specificity most directly?
options: The total volume of the cell
Its three-dimensional shape and chemical groups
questions.correctAnswer: Its three-dimensional shape and chemical groups
questions.explanation: The active site’s shape and chemical properties create complementary interactions with particular substrates.

curriculum.objective: Relate molecular structure and enzyme evidence to biological function, inhibition and reaction conditions.

questions.questionText: How can the effect of a competitive inhibitor often be reduced?
options: Lower the enzyme concentration to zero
questions.correctAnswer: Increase substrate concentration
questions.explanation: More substrate increases the chance that substrate rather than inhibitor occupies the active site.

curriculum.objective: Relate molecular structure and enzyme evidence to biological function, inhibition and reaction conditions.

questions.questionText: What is a protein’s primary structure?
options: The arrangement of several polypeptide subunits
The pattern of alpha helices only
The amino-acid sequence of its polypeptide chain
questions.correctAnswer: The amino-acid sequence of its polypeptide chain
questions.explanation: Primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

curriculum.objective: Relate molecular structure and enzyme evidence to biological function, inhibition and reaction conditions.

questions.questionText: An enzyme rate rises from 20 to 40 °C but falls steeply at 50 °C. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The tested optimum is near 40 °C and higher temperature may disrupt active-site shape
Substrate concentration must be zero at 50 °C
All enzymes have an exact optimum of 40 °C
questions.correctAnswer: The tested optimum is near 40 °C and higher temperature may disrupt active-site shape
questions.explanation: The highest tested rate occurs near 40 °C, while the fall at 50 °C is consistent with heat-induced loss of functional structure.

curriculum.objective: Relate molecular structure and enzyme evidence to biological function, inhibition and reaction conditions.

questions.questionText: Which process normally produces two genetically similar diploid daughter cells?
questions.correctAnswer: Mitosis
questions.explanation: Mitosis copies and separates chromosomes to form two daughter cells with the same chromosome number and usually the same genetic information.

curriculum.objective: Use cell division, inheritance and chromosome evidence to predict genetic outcomes and sources of variation.

questions.questionText: How does crossing over during meiosis increase variation?
options: It creates new mutations in every gene
It exchanges DNA between homologous chromosomes
questions.correctAnswer: It exchanges DNA between homologous chromosomes
questions.explanation: Exchange between homologous chromatids creates new combinations of alleles on chromosomes.

curriculum.objective: Use cell division, inheritance and chromosome evidence to predict genetic outcomes and sources of variation.

questions.questionText: What offspring ratio is expected from the test cross Aa × aa, assuming complete dominance?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 dominant : 1 recessive
questions.explanation: The heterozygote makes A and a gametes equally, while aa makes only a, producing equal Aa and aa offspring.

curriculum.objective: Use cell division, inheritance and chromosome evidence to predict genetic outcomes and sources of variation.

questions.questionText: An affected male has an X-linked recessive condition. From whom did he receive the affected X chromosome?
questions.correctAnswer: His mother
questions.explanation: A male receives his X chromosome from his mother and his Y chromosome from his father.

curriculum.objective: Use cell division, inheritance and chromosome evidence to predict genetic outcomes and sources of variation.

questions.questionText: Which feature helps a red blood cell transport oxygen efficiently?
options: A biconcave shape and abundant haemoglobin
questions.correctAnswer: A biconcave shape and abundant haemoglobin
questions.explanation: The biconcave shape increases surface-area-to-volume ratio, and haemoglobin binds oxygen while loss of the nucleus creates more space.

curriculum.objective: Analyse exchange, transport and excretory adaptations that maintain efficient organism function.

questions.questionText: What is a likely immediate effect when stomata close?
questions.correctAnswer: Water loss by transpiration decreases
questions.explanation: Closing stomata reduces diffusion of water vapour from the leaf, although it also limits carbon dioxide entry.

curriculum.objective: Analyse exchange, transport and excretory adaptations that maintain efficient organism function.

questions.questionText: How is cardiac output calculated?
questions.correctAnswer: Heart rate × stroke volume
questions.explanation: Cardiac output is the volume pumped per beat multiplied by the number of beats per unit time.

curriculum.objective: Analyse exchange, transport and excretory adaptations that maintain efficient organism function.

questions.questionText: How does the loop of Henle help produce concentrated urine?
options: It filters proteins into the nephron
It secretes glucose into the collecting duct
Countercurrent flow establishes a medullary water-potential gradient
questions.correctAnswer: Countercurrent flow establishes a medullary water-potential gradient
questions.explanation: Different permeabilities and active ion transport in opposing limbs create a medullary gradient that supports water reabsorption.

curriculum.objective: Analyse exchange, transport and excretory adaptations that maintain efficient organism function.

questions.questionText: Which method is most suitable for estimating the abundance of small plants in a field?
options: One photograph from the field edge
questions.correctAnswer: Random quadrat sampling
questions.explanation: Randomly placed quadrats provide repeatable area samples and reduce deliberate placement bias.

curriculum.objective: Interpret ecological patterns and design valid biological investigations using sampling, controls and quantitative evidence.

questions.questionText: A study finds that bird abundance and tree cover rise together. What can be concluded from correlation alone?
options: Tree cover definitely causes every increase
An association exists, but causation is not established
Birds must create the tree cover
questions.correctAnswer: An association exists, but causation is not established
questions.explanation: Correlation describes an association; other variables or reverse causation must be considered before claiming cause.

curriculum.objective: Interpret ecological patterns and design valid biological investigations using sampling, controls and quantitative evidence.

questions.questionText: Two communities have equal species richness. Which one has greater diversity?
options: The one dominated by a single species
The one with the fewest total organisms
The one with a more even distribution among species
questions.correctAnswer: The one with a more even distribution among species
questions.explanation: Diversity includes both richness and evenness, so more even relative abundances produce greater diversity when richness is equal.

curriculum.objective: Interpret ecological patterns and design valid biological investigations using sampling, controls and quantitative evidence.

questions.questionText: A hillside has strong moisture differences from top to bottom. Which sampling design best compares plant distribution along that gradient?
options: Choose sites that are easiest to reach
Use one very large quadrat at the midpoint
Place repeated quadrats systematically along transects spanning the slope
questions.correctAnswer: Place repeated quadrats systematically along transects spanning the slope
questions.explanation: Transects spanning the gradient with repeated quadrats capture ordered change while providing replication at multiple positions.

curriculum.objective: Interpret ecological patterns and design valid biological investigations using sampling, controls and quantitative evidence.
